a new aspect of the immune response in children with combinations between type 1 diabetes mellitus, coeliac disease or allergy.
the immunological interplay between common paediatric diseases and the influence of these diseases on the development of other diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

combinations of Th1‐deviations (e.g. type 1 diabetes and celiac disease) are associated with a decreased response to both allergens and antigens, whereas a combination with Th2‐deviation (e.g. allergy) is associated with an increased immune response to both allergen‐ and antigen‐specific stimuli.
combinations of paediatric immune disorders are associated with a distinct cytokine pattern, which is dependent on the combination of the diseases.

a combination of two Th2‐deviated diseases (allergy and coeliac disease, or allergy and type 1 diabetes) is associated with an increased Th2 response, whereas a Th2‐deviation (allergy) in combination with a Th1‐deviation (type 1 diabetic or coeliac disease) is associated with a reduced Th1‐response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of type 1 diabetes and allergy in children is associated with a distinct immune response to antigens associated with these diseases.
children suffering from combinations of paediatric disorders have a more pronounced and deviated immune response compared with children suffering from only one of these disorders.
children with a combination of Th2‐dominant diseases have a stronger immune response than children suffering from only one of the diseases.

the cytokine pattern in children suffering from combinations of immunological diseases differs from the cytokine pattern found in children with only one of the diseases, which may be of importance in the understanding of disease pathogenesis.
